description: Feature A — the 'Enable location' strip above Start drive. Add a full-width informational/action strip as the first child of #panel-footer, directly above #start-drive. Hidden when permission is 'granted' (or 'unsupported'); shown for 'prompt' and 'denied'. In 'prompt' it triggers the native prompt via KPR.map.requestLocation(); in 'denied' it reveals inline, device-specific re-enable steps (iOS Safari path vs generic site-settings) and never re-prompts. It reacts live via KPR.geoPermission.subscribe so granting (from anywhere) hides it. Styled with existing Ocean theme vars so it is visually distinct from the primary Start drive button. Depends on FEAT-001 (uses KPR.geoPermission and KPR.map.requestLocation()).
steps:
In index.html, inside #panel-footer, add as the FIRST child (before #start-drive):
containing a full-width

In css/style.css, add styles using ONLY existing theme vars: .enable-location { grid-column: 1 / -1; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px; padding: 10px 12px; background: var(--surface-2); border: 1px solid var(--line-strong); border-left: 3px solid var(--warn); border-radius: var(--radius-md); color: var(--text); } — clearly NOT the violet .drive-btn. Style #enable-location-btn as a modest full-width action (text-align:left or centered, font-weight 600, color var(--text) with the glyph/accent in var(--accent) or var(--warn)); it must NOT look like .drive-btn (no big violet fill, no large shadow). .enable-location-help { font-size: 12px; line-height: 1.5; color: var(--text-muted); } with finger-friendly spacing. Rely on the existing .hidden { display:none } to hide the strip and the help sub-region. Add a padding/size tweak under the existing @media (max-width: 900px) block only if needed to match footer padding.

Create js/enable-location-strip.js as an IIFE KPR.enableLocationStrip with init() and an exported render(state) (export render so tests can call it directly, mirroring how browse-routes exports renderList).

init(): look up the strip elements once; add a click listener to #enable-location-btn (handler uses the CURRENT KPR.geoPermission.getState()); subscribe to KPR.geoPermission.subscribe(render); and call render(KPR.geoPermission.getState()) once for the initial paint.

render(state): if state is 'granted' or 'unsupported', add 'hidden' to #enable-location and also hide #enable-location-help; if 'prompt' or 'denied', remove 'hidden' from #enable-location. In 'prompt': set the button label to 'Enable location' and keep #enable-location-help hidden. In 'denied': keep the button present (label may stay 'Enable location' or become 'Location is blocked — how to fix'); the help stays hidden until the button is tapped.

Button click handler: if state is 'prompt', call KPR.map.requestLocation() (triggers the native popup); the subsequent permissions 'change' event will re-run render and hide the strip once granted. If state is 'denied', toggle #enable-location-help visible and fill it (textContent only, no innerHTML) with device-specific steps: KPR.geoPermission.isIOS() -> 'Settings › Privacy › Location Services › Safari Websites', else 'Allow location for this site in your browser's site settings, then reload.' Do NOT call requestLocation() when denied (no re-prompt loop).

Add <script src="js/enable-location-strip.js"></script> to index.html AFTER js/drive.js, and call KPR.enableLocationStrip.init() from the app startup path alongside the other module init() calls (follow where sibling modules like browse-routes/start-chooser are initialized — e.g. in KPR.app.init or the same place drive/evaluation init run).

In tests/run.html: add a fixture DOM block replicating the footer strip — a #panel-footer-ish container holding #enable-location (with #enable-location-btn and #enable-location-help) and a #start-drive stub button — using the same ids/classes as index.html. Add <script src="../js/enable-location-strip.js"></script> to the script list (after the app modules).

Create tests/enable-location.test.js mirroring tests/browse-routes.test.js. Stub KPR.map (e.g. window.KPR.map = { requestLocation: spy }) and drive KPR.geoPermission state via the seam established in FEAT-001 (or stub getState/isIOS directly on the KPR.geoPermission object for the render/click tests). Assert: render('granted') and render('unsupported') hide #enable-location; render('prompt') and render('denied') show it; clicking the button in 'prompt' calls the KPR.map.requestLocation spy; clicking in 'denied' reveals #enable-location-help, fills it with the iOS text when isIOS() is true and the generic text when false, and does NOT call requestLocation.
Register tests/enable-location.test.js at the end of the tests/run.html <script> list.
acceptance_criteria: In index.html, #enable-location is the first child of #panel-footer, above #start-drive, and spans the grid row.
The strip is visually distinct from .drive-btn (uses --surface-2 background / --warn accent, not the violet nav-fill) and uses only existing theme vars.
render('granted') and render('unsupported') hide the strip; render('prompt') and render('denied') show it.
Clicking the strip in 'prompt' calls KPR.map.requestLocation(); clicking in 'denied' reveals inline device-specific text (iOS vs generic) via textContent and does not call requestLocation().
Running the test command ends with RESULT: PASS and a total count greater than the post-FEAT-001 count, with the enable-location tests listed as ok.
verification: Run: powershell -NoProfile -File tests\run-tests.ps1 — confirm 'RESULT: PASS (N tests)' with N greater than the FEAT-001 total and the enable-location tests showing 'ok'.
Confirm the DOM-safety audit (tests/render-audit.test.js) still passes, verifying the strip help text uses textContent not innerHTML.
findings:

Wired in js/app.js init() between KPR.drive.init() and KPR.results.init(). render(state) -> EXPORTED (like browse-routes.renderList) so tests call it directly. 'granted'|'unsupported' add 'hidden' to #enable-location AND hide+clear #enable-location-help; 'prompt'|'denied' remove 'hidden' from #enable-location and (re)collapse the help sub-region.
